sermon.title: We Have an Enemy
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 59:19 that the enemy comes in like a flood and the Spirit of the Lord lifts up a standard against him. He lists philosophies he says oppose God, then shows from Genesis and the flood that God makes a way of escape, and urges the church to warn people.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he cites “Luke 16:26” for the story of Lazarus and the rich man; the whole account (Luke 16:19-31) is linked. He cites “Matthew 25:46 and 1916” (Matthew 19:16). The phrases “fair share,” “slave to welfare,” and the statistics he gives (such as 2%, 16%, 23%, 15% and 75%) are his own statements as spoken; they are not checked here. In the section on opposing philosophies he refers to a sitting U.S. President by name, to political parties, immigration, abortion-adjacent topics, homosexuality, evolution and public schools; names appear in the transcript only, not in the short answers. A quote he attributes to a homosexual activist contains a profanity, written [expletive] (near 16:49). Real people named in the transcript only: a sitting U.S. President (near 9:31), Harry Truman (near 38:52), a preacher by first name (near 41:19) and a staff member by first name (near 37:42). A garbled phrase near 11:22 (about a person he compares to “science”) and one word each near 18:42 and 37:42 are marked [unclear]. The fire story near 38:00 is about a wildfire near his property.

chunks.section_question: What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?
chunks.short_answer: He says there is “an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word,” and a flood “does nothing but damage.” He says the church is “trying to do this stuff on their own,” but the key to defeating the enemy is the Spirit: “the Spirit will lift up a standard against him.”
chunks.text:
We neglect, we disregard many priority doctrines, and one of these is Isaiah 59:19. Isaiah 59:19 says, “When the enemy comes in like a flood.” Number one, the enemy. We have an enemy. There is an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word, and when the enemy comes in like a flood (and all of us know a flood does nothing but damage; when you hear the word “flood,” you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control). Secondly, “the Spirit of the Lord will lift up a...” The Spirit of the Lord. Now, folks, this is where we’re missing it. The church is trying to do this stuff on their own. If we could have done it on our own, why we have needed Jesus?

Why would we need the Holy Ghost? And it’s amazing, we start out right, we get saved and we start out right, and then we start leaning on ourself and on our own knowledge and understanding, but the key to defeating the enemy is what? The Spirit. The Spirit that everybody in America is arguing about, that’s the very part of God that will defeat your enemies. Good place for an amen. Amen means so be it. How many need your enemies defeated? Yeah, opposition. Yes, and they’re bigger than you are. You know, “the Spirit will lift up a standard against him.” Now, the word “standard” is not talking about a banner. There, when we worshiped God this morning and they talked about raising the banner, you notice I went over and got a banner, and the song said to raise the banner, so I, “Give me a banner.” I don’t have to wait for permission. They got the song, I just do what it says. Can I hear an amen? You say, “Well, that might not be in order.” Well, then don’t sing the song.

chunks.section_question: What does “the Spirit will lift up a standard” mean, and does God make a way of escape?
chunks.short_answer: He says “standard” has two meanings: to flee or escape, and to attack the enemy. He says whether God flees the enemy or causes you to flee, “He is going to move on your behalf,” and that “there is no temptation come upon anybody” that God will not make a way of escape from.
chunks.text:
If you don’t want me lifting up a banner, then don’t sing the song. You don’t want me dancing, then don’t sing a song that says dance. Because this guy has learned the key is to obey the Scriptures, not just sing them, not just memorize them, but obey them. Is that a good place for us? So be it. Yeah. Now, the standard here has two meanings. You know, just like the word “bear,” b-e-a-r, in our language has several meanings: bear, an animal, grizzly bear, brown bear. It also means to carry: “I will bear that.” It also means falling prices: we got a bear market or a bear economy, things are falling down. Or it means to produce fruit. Jesus said, “I wish that you bear fruit and that your fruit remain.” See, it’s producing something. And so the standard here has two meanings: to flee, to escape, to take flight, to depart (and, uh, that’s us escaping from the enemy). The second meaning is different: it’s attacking the enemy. It means to fly to the attack, to put to flight. See, and the Spirit is going to lift up a standard against who? The enemy, him, the enemy.

And He’s going to make a way of escape. And you know, the Bible says in the New Testament that there is no temptation come upon anybody that’s not common to man, that God will make a way of escape that you might bear up under it. You can handle it. Whether God flees the enemy or whether God causes you to flee, He is going to move on your behalf. All right, we got that part now. See, what’s the important thing in this verse? The Spirit. I can’t do this. I learned as a young believer I couldn’t do this stuff on my own. You know, as a young believer people would make fun of me because I claimed to be a Christian and I was making mistakes. Say, “I said I’m going to go to church with a bunch of hypocrites anyway.” I said, “Well, at least we’re going.” I said, “Is a Marine, when he enters the base the first day, is he really a Marine? The next week, is he a Marine? The next two weeks, is he a Marine?” No, he’s not a Marine till he passes and gets the standard, the U.S. standard, to be a Marine. He’s a Marine. I said, “Yes, we’re in church, and we’re learning how to be a Christian, but at least we’re there learning.” Can I hear an amen? Yeah. We got our flaws, we got our m— but we’re there, we’re trying to be like Him. We want that stamp to be like Him.

chunks.section_question: Who do we wrestle against, and what does he say about atheists? (Ephesians 6:12)
chunks.short_answer: He says we are attacking the philosophies, not the people: “we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers,” the principles of men that try to capture our mind. He then lists the first opposing philosophy, atheism, saying that “when you speak something that’s against God, you are an enemy.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. Now, we need that standard lifted up in America. We have more than seven opposing philosophies. It’s the philosophies that we are attacking back. It’s the philosophies that we need to lift up a standard against. It’s not the people. “We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers and spiritual wickedness in high places.” We wrestle against the principles of men that try to capture our mind. Paul said a person can be a good person, but if he’s got a few flaws, he’s opposing God. We have to, with the Word, try to correct that stuff. Can I hear an amen? And so first we have the atheists, who don’t believe there is a God. They say there is no God. There’s 2% of the population is atheist. How many percent? 2%. Did they get the Bible out of public schools? Yeah. You call that a democracy? 2% got the Bible out of public schools. That’s not a democracy. A democracy is the majority rules.

Just letting you think all right. They say that humanity is the absolute total source of ethics and values. Individuals themselves can resolve moral problems. We don’t need a God. There is no life after death, there is no lake of fire, there is no judgment after death, you just go to the grave, and there are some churches who believe that nonsense. All right, atheist. So that opposes God. See, when you speak something that’s against God, you are an enemy, you are opposing, you hate God, and that’s when I’m out there debating you, who hear me lift my voice and I tell them like it is: “You are haters.” Why? Because they’re opposing God. “You are bashers.” Why? They’re bashing the Bible. They’re bashing. I just tell them what they are. I’m just telling them the truth. “Well, as Christians, you shouldn’t do that.” Oh, and where do you find that twisted scripture in the Bible? Are you out there? You may not be able to reach your enemy, but those that hear you may get convicted and learn and change. All right, then we have the hedonist. Pleasure is the highest good. Whatever causes pleasure is right. Whatever makes you happy is right.

He says church liberals deny that Jesus is God and born of a virgin.

chunks.short_answer: He says only 15% of Americans believe in evolution, according to a poll he cites, and that evolutionists “say the Bible’s a lie.” He says Christians “have to oppose that philosophy that destroys people’s life” and “come back with God’s philosophy that sets people free,” and that “they have a right to freedom of speech, we have a right to freedom of speech.”
chunks.text:
So the evolution is, of course, there’s 15%. I did not know this, this was new to me. A Gallup poll just taken in 2012: only 15% of Americans believe in evolution. I was shocked. The way they projected, I thought 80%. Dead. Isn’t that a good one? We ought to be excited about that. Most Americans aren’t falling for that lie. Yeah. And basically they say the Bible’s a lie, that God did not create the world, it just spontaneously happened, and we don’t know where the first molecule or the first atom or the first cell came from, but this is the way it happened. And so they are opponents of God. Now, so here we are: atheists, no God; hedonists, sex, drugs, parties, feels good, do it; liberals, church and secular; humanists, no God again; evolutionists say the Bible’s a lie; homosexuals say they can’t change.

They bash Jesus, they say the Bible is a book of myths. In fact, one of the big homosexual activists said the Bible is BS, it is a book of bull [expletive]. That’s what he said, and they openly say that. And then the Christians want to be nice little people. “Well, we love you.” No, we have to oppose that philosophy that destroys people’s life. We got to come back with God’s philosophy that sets people free. Amen. And I don’t have to go, “Oh, God loves you.” I can talk to them straight, just like they talk to the American people straight. They have a right to freedom of speech, we have a right to freedom of speech. We have a right to say what God said. They have a right to say their own lies if they want to. We’re in America. Are you with me?

chunks.section_question: Why must the church keep warning people, and does it matter how it is said?
chunks.short_answer: He says the burden is to get the Word out and “warn them,” and that “it doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to.” He tells a story of a police officer telling him to evacuate a fire, and says people should not turn off a message because of how it is delivered, since “it’s the message that will set you free.”
chunks.text:
Amen. And so we have a burden on us to get the Word of God out, and we need, every year I’m saying this, and we’re still not getting the Word of God out like we should: the printed word, the audible word, the video word, the Internet word. We need to take on [unclear] personally and get the word out to them, warn them. And then some people say, “Well, it’s all in how you say it.” Well, let me give you a little illustration here. At this fire that came over this property, we evacuated the kids from the school. Christina was on the ball and had the kids out by 12:30 or so. We took the horses out. I had the tractor down there scraping down the brush behind the house. I didn’t want the house to burn down. That fire is coming over that mountain, and it’s moving pretty quick, you know, covering a mile in two hours is pretty fast, and that fire is about 300 feet from me, and I’m still knocking down this brush.

And one of the firemen comes over and says, “Sir, you did a great job, you’ve saved the building, but it’s time to go.” And he said it with empathy, with feeling, and I already knew it. It’s time to go. I already had my exit route planned out. I, the, the, the gas, the smoke was up here in the air, it wasn’t down here where you’re breathing, so you could last a lot longer. If that smoke would have dropped, I’d have been out of there early. How many know that? But anyway, he was right. He said it nice and politely. I didn’t have to leave the property, just like Harry Truman at Mount St. Helens, when they told him to leave his property, the Mount St. Helens was going to erupt. He said, “I ain’t leaving here, I lived here all my life, I’m going to die here,” and he stayed there and he died, and I could have stayed there. Well, anyway, I go around and I drop the tractor off, and I come around, and this guy pulls up in a car, and he says, “You got to evacuate now,” and I go, “Who are you?”

I said, “Are you the fire department?” He said, “No, I’m a police officer.” I go, “Oh,” and I kept on doing what I was doing, and he says, I said, “You got to leave now.” I didn’t even pay him any mind. He was grouchy, grumpy, authoritative, and anything else, but I know who I am, and I know my rights, and I know what I got to get done. I had three more things to get done. I was going to get them done. Now, I could have been stupid and said, “Well, if that’s the way he’s going to talk to me, I’m not leaving, I’ll show him,” and I could have burned with him. He didn’t talk to me right. How many know, folks, it doesn’t matter how we say it, it’s still the truth, and you better listen. You know, if your mentality is, “Well, talk to me, say please, and I’ll listen,” grow up. Not all of us are going to talk to you the sweet way: “You poor little thing, we don’t want to hurt your feelings, but you’re going to hell.” Oh God, you’re going to hell. We may say, “Idiot, turn or burn.” It doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to. Can I hear an amen?

It doesn’t matter if you’re there smiling like Joel, smiling, never, never misses a smile. I’d like to see him in real life. You got it. Folks, don’t turn off the message because a tooth is missing in someone, or they can’t say the English language right, or they may say it harshly, or they may say it whiny. The thing is, listen to the message. It’s the message that will set you free. “Smoking: Surgeon General’s warning: causes cancer, heart disease, emphysema, and may complicate pregnancy.” It doesn’t “may” now, it is affecting your baby, they know that. Now, is there a protest on Washington to take that label off? No. Is the atheist offended by that and said, “You know, get that label off, you’re offending us, you’re taking away our right to kill ourself and get cancer”? Is the homosexuals rallying to get rid of that? No. But they don’t like God telling them what to do. They don’t like God telling them that He wants to rule over their life. Amen.

Now, if I was a smoker, that would be offensive to me. I mean, you know, millions of Americans don’t pay any attention to that warning, and it’s there every pack you get, it’s there every carton you get, it’s there. Church, should we keep on warning just because they don’t listen? Should we keep telling? Yes, and that’s what we got to get done this year. We got to get the word out, the word of righteousness, and let God raise up a standard and defeat the enemy in people’s life and give them a way of escape, that they can have a new life in Christ Jesus. Amen. That’s our job. That’s what we got to do. So today, are you in love with Jesus? Are you going to love Jesus, accepting and living by the standards of Bible morality? And are you going to admonish, instruct, and warn and notify and advise, the best of your ability? Don’t worry about how you say it. How many just say, “I’m going to give it a shot”? Would you raise your hand? Yeah. Your approach may be all messed up, but you’ll learn. You’ll learn by giving it a shot.

faqs.question: What does the “flood” mean in Isaiah 59:19?
faqs.answer: He says “a flood does nothing but damage. When you hear the word ‘flood,’ you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control,” and the enemy comes in that way.

scriptures.text_nkjv: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.

faqs.question: What does he say is the key to defeating the enemy?
faqs.answer: He says it is “the Spirit… the very part of God that will defeat your enemies,” rather than leaning “on our own knowledge and understanding.”

faqs.question: What are the two meanings of “standard” in Isaiah 59:19?
faqs.answer: He says one is “to flee, to escape, to take flight,” and the other is “attacking the enemy,” to “fly to the attack, to put to flight.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.

faqs.question: What does he say the Bible promises about temptation?
faqs.answer: He says there is “no temptation come upon anybody” that God will not make “a way of escape that you might bear up under it.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.

faqs.question: What is his “finger in the socket” illustration?
faqs.answer: He says most Pentecostals “only experience putting our finger in the socket. We didn’t learn how to channel it,” but “at least we felt the power of God, right?” and “then we can learn how to channel it.”

faqs.question: Who does he say we wrestle against?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s not the people. We wrestle not against flesh and blood… we wrestle against the principles of men that try to capture our mind.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.

faqs.question: What does he say about people who follow their denomination above the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says a religionist “will defend their denomination above Jesus Christ Himself and the Bible,” and asks, “We’re not told to follow a man. Who are we told to follow? Jesus.”

faqs.question: Did God kill Adam and Eve as He said He would?
faqs.answer: He says no: “He didn’t kill Adam and Eve like He said He would,” but gave “a way of escape.” He says he asks this to show God is the same “yesterday, today, and forever.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

faqs.question: Why does he say God shed an animal’s blood for Adam and Eve?
faqs.answer: He says it was “the first written illustration of God’s plan,” and “God already knew He was going to die for the sins of the world.” He says “the Bible says His blood was shed before the foundation of the world.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Also for Adam and his wife the LORD God made tunics of skin, and clothed them.

faqs.question: Why does he say God said “woman” in Genesis 3:15?
faqs.answer: He says “all through the Bible His people, God’s church, is an allegory of a bride,” and that God “didn’t say Adam, He said woman.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I will put enmity Between you and the woman, And between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, And you shall bruise His heel.”

faqs.question: How many converts did Noah have?
faqs.answer: He says Noah “only had seven converts: his wife, his three boys, and three girls,” after preaching righteousness for 100 years. He says Noah was successful “because he did what God told him to do. You’re not measured by numbers.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence. So God looked upon the earth, and indeed it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth. And God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

faqs.question: How does the Bible show it is God’s word, according to him?
faqs.answer: He says God named Babylon, Persia and Greece and predicted what they would do “hundreds of years before they were a nation, and they did it,” and that “only God can tell what the future holds and bring it to pass.”

faqs.question: What does he say Jesus told the man who asked about eternal life?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus told him, “If you will enter into life, keep the commandments,” and then listed the commandments about how we treat others, ending with “you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”

faqs.question: What did the rich man in hell ask for?
faqs.answer: He says he asked for Lazarus to dip his finger in water to cool his tongue, and then asked that Lazarus be sent to warn his brothers “lest they too come into this place of torment.”
